events.title: Firefox 6 released
events.summary: Mozilla released Firefox 6 on August 16, 2011 — continuing the rapid-release cycle with faster startup, improved dev tools, and Panorama tab groups.
events.about: Firefox 6 refined the six-week release model Mozilla started with version 5: incremental security fixes, WebSockets support, and better permissions UI. It kept Firefox competitive while Chrome's market share climbed.

narrative.whyChosen: Firefox 6 solidified Mozilla's rapid-release cadence for the 2010s.
narrative.whyImportant: Frequent releases brought security patches and web APIs to users faster.
narrative.problemSolved: Long gaps between major Firefox versions left users exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities.

events.title: Swagger 1.0 released
events.summary: Tony Tam released Swagger 1.0 on August 10, 2011 — a machine-readable format for describing REST APIs and generating client SDKs.
events.about: Swagger (later OpenAPI) documents endpoints, parameters, and response schemas in JSON or YAML — powering interactive docs, code generators, and API gateways. Tools like Swagger UI render `try it out` consoles from the same spec. Example: a `GET /users/{id}` path with typed parameters becomes a typed TypeScript client automatically.

narrative.whyChosen: Swagger 1.0 was the first widely adopted REST API description format.
narrative.whyImportant: It made API contracts machine-readable and spawned the OpenAPI ecosystem.
narrative.problemSolved: REST APIs were documented in prose; clients and servers drifted without a shared schema.

events.title: Marc Andreessen: "Software is eating the world"
events.summary: In a Wall Street Journal essay, Marc Andreessen argues that every industry is becoming a software business.
events.about: Written at the height of the mobile and cloud boom, the line justified VC bets on Uber, Airbnb, and SaaS eating hotels, taxis, and shrink-wrapped software. It aged into a cliché — because it was largely right.

narrative.whyChosen: The thesis statement of the 2010s startup era.
narrative.whyImportant: It reframed non-tech industries as software delivery problems.
narrative.problemSolved: Investors and incumbents underestimated how fast software would disrupt physical businesses.

sources.title: Wall Street Journal — Why Software Is Eating the World (August 20, 2011)
